name: Tokyo Dome City Attractions
description: An urban amusement park complex connected to a massive indoor mall. Home to Thunder Dolphin roller coaster, a Ferris wheel with stunning city views, a splash pad for hot days, and Tokyo's largest roller skating rink.
tipsAndTricks: Buy the 'Free Pass' wristband for unlimited rides if your kid is over 110cm. Shorter kids pay per ride and it's cheaper.
Thunder Dolphin is 80 meters tall and scary for young kids. Start with the Ferris wheel first to gauge their comfort with heights.
The roller skating rink has penguin-shaped walkers that toddlers can push. Our 3-year-old was skating within 10 minutes.
Combine with the Tokyo Dome Hotel's kids' buffet next door. It's a 5-minute walk and has a low-price lunch special.
Rainy days are fine here — half the attractions are indoors and the mall connects everything under cover.

parentStory.title: The ride that made my 5-year-old fearless
parentStory.excerpt: She was terrified of the kiddie coaster until a staff member let her stand beside it and watch the train come in three times. Then she marched onto the ride like a little warrior.
parentStory.author: Yuki, mom of 2 from Tokyo
parentStory.fullStory: We live 20 minutes from Tokyo Dome City but never went because I assumed it was for older kids. Then a friend dragged us there on a rainy Saturday. The 'Wonder Drop' splash pad was a hit, but the real surprise was the Wonder Coaster — a tiny train-style roller coaster. My 5-year-old was too scared to try, and a ride attendant spent 10 minutes patiently talking her through it. She rode it six times after that.

itineraryComparison.halfDay: 3-4 rides + Ferris wheel + lunch, 3 hours total
itineraryComparison.fullDay: All rides + roller skating + spa at Tokyo Dome Hotel
itineraryComparison.bestFor: Ages 4-12, families who want theme park fun without the Disney price tag

name: Inokashira Park & Zoo
description: A charming petite zoo inside a vast park with a pond, paddle boats, and a Ghibli Museum just steps away. The zoo is compact enough for toddlers, featuring small mammals, birds, and a petting area with guinea pigs.
bestTime: Early morning weekends or weekday mornings
tipsAndTricks: The zoo costs only 500 yen for adults and is FREE for kids under 12.
Go counter-clockwise through the park — the Ghibli Museum is at the south end and tickets sell out weeks in advance, so plan that separately.
The guinea pig petting area opens at 10:30 AM and limits visits to 15 minutes. Line up by 10:15.
Paddle boats on the pond cost 700 yen for 30 minutes. Our 4-year-old was enchanted by the turtles swimming alongside.
Don't bother with the zoo cafe. The park has excellent vending machines and you're 10 minutes from Kichijoji's great kid-friendly restaurants.

parentStory.title: Cheaper than a coffee, better than a theme park
parentStory.excerpt: We spent 500 yen and 3 hours here. My toddler fed the koi, petted a guinea pig, and we paddled around the pond under cherry blossoms. It was the cheapest day of our Tokyo trip and her absolute favorite.
parentStory.author: Claire, mom of 1 from Vancouver
parentStory.fullStory: After two days of expensive theme parks, our daughter was overstimulated and exhausted. Inokashira Park was the reset we needed. The zoo is tiny but perfectly scaled for little legs. She ran ahead on every path because we could see her the whole time. We paddle-boated, ate melon pan from a street vendor, and watched the swan boats bump into each other.

itineraryComparison.halfDay: Zoo + petting area + paddle boats + park stroll, 3-4 hours
itineraryComparison.fullDay: Add Ghibli Museum + lunch in Kichijoji for a full day out

name: Edo-Tokyo Museum
description: A stunning museum recreating Tokyo's evolution from a small fishing village to a mega-city. Features life-sized replica buildings, a full-scale Nihonbashi bridge you can walk across, and hands-on exhibits with kimono dressing and calligraphy.
bestTime: Weekday mornings, especially Wednesday (fewer school groups)
tipsAndTricks: Rent the English tablet guide for 500 yen. It turns every exhibit into a story.
The real kabuki theater replica on the 6th floor has a 20-minute video show — a great break for tired legs.
Don't miss the 'Hands-On Corner' on the 5th floor. Kids can try on samurai helmets and kimono for free.
The museum is closed on Mondays. Check the calendar for exhibit change closures.
Combine with the nearby Sumo Museum (Ryogoku Kokugikan). It's a 5-minute walk and free entry.

parentStory.title: The samurai helmet that stayed on for 30 minutes
parentStory.excerpt: My 7-year-old put on a samurai helmet in the hands-on corner and refused to take it off. A volunteer showed him how to hold a fake katana. History for the dinner table — that's what this museum delivered.
parentStory.author: Paul, dad of 2 from San Diego
parentStory.fullStory: I expected a boring history museum. My daughter expected to be bored. We were both wrong. The life-sized Edo-period town with the Nihonbashi bridge blew her away. The 3D map of Tokyo's firebombing in 1945 was sobering but handled well — no gore, just scale. We spent 3 hours there and only left because we were hungry.

itineraryComparison.halfDay: Main exhibits + hands-on corner + cafe, 2.5-3 hours
itineraryComparison.fullDay: Add Sumo Museum + chanko nabe lunch in Ryogoku + river cruise
itineraryComparison.bestFor: School-age kids who love history, ages 7-15

name: Toei Kyoto Studio Park
description: A working film studio and theme park where samurai dramas are filmed live. Kids watch ninja shows, explore Edo-period streets built for movies, dress up in kimonos, and even try wire-flying stunts.
bestTime: Weekdays, avoid Japanese national holidays when school groups swarm
tipsAndTricks: The ninja show gets packed 20 minutes before showtime. Sit on the left side — that's where ninjas enter and kids get the best view.
Rent the ninja costume for your kid (1,000 yen). They'll wear it all day.
Wire-flying has a height minimum of 120cm. Offer the samurai costume as a backup for shorter kids.
Skip the sit-down restaurant. Edo-period street food like mitarashi dango and takoyaki is everywhere.
Studio tours happen at 11 AM and 2 PM. The guide speaks Japanese but the visuals are entertaining regardless.

parentStory.title: When a ninja 'attacked' our table during lunch
parentStory.excerpt: We were eating soba when a real actor in full ninja gear leaped onto our table and posed for photos. My son's jaw dropped. He still tells everyone about the time a real ninja ate lunch with us.
parentStory.author: Mark, dad of 1 from Sydney
parentStory.fullStory: Toei is chaotic in the best way. No scripted schedule like Disney — actors roam and improvise. A samurai challenged my wife to a pretend duel while she was holding matcha. The ninja show blew my mind with real wire work. For a kid who loves action movies, this beats any theme park.

itineraryComparison.halfDay: Ninja show + wire-flying + costume rental + Edo street, 3 hours
itineraryComparison.fullDay: All shows + studio tour + outdoor film set exploration

name: Kyoto City Zoo
description: Japan's second-oldest zoo, recently renovated with modern open habitats. Compact enough for toddlers, featuring elephants, giraffes, and a children's corner where kids can pet goats and rabbits. Cherry blossom trees in spring make it picture-perfect.
bestTime: Early morning, cherry blossom season (late March-April)
tipsAndTricks: Entry is just 600 yen for adults and FREE for kids under 15.
The petting corner opens at 10 AM and closes at 3 PM. Go there FIRST — by 11 AM the goats get full and stop interacting.
Combine with Heian Jingu Shrine and the Modern Art Museum — both a 5-minute walk away in Okazaki Park.
The zoo is small. Think of it as a lovely 90-minute pitstop, not a day trip.
The playground near the main entrance has a massive wooden jungle gym.

parentStory.title: A zoo that respects your Saturday
parentStory.excerpt: We had only 90 minutes before our temple reservation. Kyoto Zoo was perfect — compact, uncrowded, and our toddler could see every animal without squinting.
parentStory.author: Emily, mom of 2 from Portland
parentStory.fullStory: We were debating between Kyoto Zoo and Osaka Aquarium. So glad we picked the zoo. The petting corner was wonderfully calm — staff limit how many kids enter at once. My 3-year-old spent 20 minutes brushing a goat and naming it 'Fluffy.' Being in the Okazaki cultural district means you seamlessly move on to temples or museums.

itineraryComparison.halfDay: Zoo + petting corner + Heian Jingu + canal-side lunch
itineraryComparison.fullDay: Zoo morning + Kyoto Museum of Traditional Crafts + Philosopher's Path afternoon
itineraryComparison.bestFor: Ages 0-8, quick outings in central Kyoto

name: Osaka Aquarium Kaiyukan
description: One of the world's most impressive aquariums, centered around a massive 9-meter deep Pacific Ocean tank with whale sharks gliding overhead. The spiral ramp design lets kids walk through 15 exhibits at their own pace, from Antarctic penguins to Japanese forest otters.
bestTime: Weekday openings, avoid rainy weekends when locals pack in
tipsAndTricks: Go up the escalator to the 8th floor FIRST, then walk down the spiral. Everyone else goes the opposite direction.
The whale shark tank reveals something new at every level — top: dorsal view, middle: side view, bottom: from below.
Touch pool with stingrays opens at 10:30 AM. Go before 11 AM or skip it.
Buy tickets online the night before. On-site queues can be 45 minutes on weekends.
Combine with Tempozan Ferris Wheel (right next door, 800 yen) and Legoland Discovery Center across the street.

parentStory.title: The whale shark that made her believe in magic
parentStory.excerpt: My 4-year-old pressed her hands to the glass and whispered 'Mama, it's bigger than our car.' The whale shark slowly turned and swam past again. She believed in magic that day.
parentStory.author: Hana, mom of 1 from Seoul
parentStory.fullStory: I've been to the Georgia Aquarium and the one in Dubai. Kaiyukan is different. The spiral descent makes every reveal feel cinematic — you don't see the whale shark until you're standing at the main tank on the 4th floor. My daughter spent 25 minutes at that single pane of glass.

itineraryComparison.halfDay: Aquarium only, 2-3 hours including touch pool
itineraryComparison.fullDay: Aquarium + Legoland Discovery + Ferris wheel + Tempozan Harbor Village lunch
itineraryComparison.bestFor: Ages 2-14, ocean lovers, rainy day backup plan

name: Tennoji Zoo
description: Osaka's historic city zoo set inside sprawling Tennoji Park. Home to lions, elephants, koalas, and a popular reptile house. Newer 'Open Habitat' zones reduce barriers for clearer views. The adjacent Tennoji Park has a massive playground and pond.
bestTime: Weekday mornings, October-December when animals are most active
tipsAndTricks: Entry is 500 yen for adults, FREE for kids under 15. Perfect for a budget family afternoon.
The koala house is the most popular exhibit — line up early because koalas are most active in the cool morning.
The Open Habitat zone (renovated 2022) has no bars, just glass and moats. Much better photos.
Tennoji Park next door has a free splash pad that runs June-September. Bring swimsuits in summer.
Don't skip the insectarium — kids can hold beetles and stick insects under supervision.

parentStory.title: 500 yen for a koala wake-up show
parentStory.excerpt: We arrived at 9:30 AM and saw a koala stretch, yawn, and shuffle from one branch to another. My 3-year-old shrieked with joy. 500 yen for that moment? Unbeatable.
parentStory.author: Tom, dad of 1 from Hawaii
parentStory.fullStory: Tennoji Zoo gets a bad rap because it's old (1915). But recent renovations have transformed it. The old concrete cages are gone. The koalas are genuinely happy — I've never seen them so active. The playground in Tennoji Park is enormous and shaded, so we spent as much time there as at the zoo.

itineraryComparison.halfDay: Zoo + Tennoji Park playground + lunch at Abeno Harukas
itineraryComparison.fullDay: Add Osaka Museum of History and Shitennoji Temple

name: Nagoya Port Aquarium
description: One of Japan's largest aquariums divided into two pavilions: the Journey of the Antarctic featuring orcas and dolphins, and the Sea of Japan with native species. Famous for orca training shows, a massive dolphin stadium, and an open-ocean tank with whale sharks and manta rays.
bestTime: Weekdays, show schedules run every 40 minutes
tipsAndTricks: Download the show schedule PDF before you go. The orca show fills up 30 minutes early on weekends.
North Pavilion (Journey of the Antarctic) is quieter — most crowds go to the dolphin show first.
The orca training pool viewing window is on the 3rd floor. Get there 15 minutes before training at 11 AM.
Consider a baby carrier — escalators between floors get crowded after shows.
Combine with the Port of Nagoya Maritime Museum and the Sky Tower Ferris wheel for a full-day outing.

parentStory.title: The orca that waved back at my daughter
parentStory.excerpt: During training, an orca lifted its pectoral fin and 'waved' at the audience. My 6-year-old waved back frantically. She's convinced they made a connection.
parentStory.author: Lea, mom of 2 from Berlin
parentStory.fullStory: We drove from Tokyo specifically for this aquarium. The orca show is more educational than performative — explaining hunting behaviors, social structures, and conservation. The touch pool with small sharks was a hit. Only downside: bring your own lunch — the cafe is mediocre and expensive.

itineraryComparison.fullDay: Add Port Museum + Ferris wheel + Nagoya City Science Museum
itineraryComparison.bestFor: Ages 3-14, marine life fans, day-trippers from Tokyo/Osaka

name: Kenrokuen Garden Family Walk
description: One of Japan's three great landscape gardens, meticulously designed with ponds, streams, teahouses, and iconic stone lanterns. Wide gravel paths, plenty of benches, and a legendary fountain powered by natural water pressure. Each season transforms the garden — from plum blossoms in February to fiery maples in November.
tipsAndTricks: Enter from Kodatsuno Gate (upper entrance). It's less crowded and slopes DOWN, easier with strollers.
The Kasumigaike Pond walking path lets kids run freely because you can always see them across the water.
Buy the matcha set at Shigure-tei teahouse (700 yen). Kids' matcha comes with a sweet bean cake.
Go early (8:30 AM opening). By 10 AM tour buses arrive.
Exit through Ishigawa-mon gate to Kanazawa Castle Park — a great spot to let kids run wild after the garden's quiet rules.

parentStory.title: She saw the fountain and asked why no one turned it off
parentStory.excerpt: My 5-year-old stared at the natural fountain for 10 minutes trying to find the plug. When I explained it's gravity-powered, she said 'Can we stay and watch?' We stayed 20 more minutes.
parentStory.author: Akiko, mom of 2 from Nagoya
parentStory.fullStory: I was nervous about bringing young kids to a cultural garden. They loved it more than the castle. The wide paths let them walk without holding hands, the koi fish kept them occupied, and the teahouse was a perfect mid-walk break. We spent 2.5 hours here and nobody complained.

itineraryComparison.halfDay: Garden walk + teahouse + castle park, 2-3 hours
itineraryComparison.fullDay: Garden morning + Kanazawa Castle + Ninjadera temple + sake brewery tour
itineraryComparison.bestFor: All ages, nature lovers, families seeking a calm cultural morning

name: Ishikawa Prefectural Museum
description: A modern museum showcasing Ishikawa's rich traditional crafts — gold leaf (Kanazawa is famous for it), Kaga yuzen silk dyeing, kutani porcelain, and Wajima lacquerware. Interactive sections let kids try gold leaf application and watch live craft demonstrations.
tipsAndTricks: The gold leaf application workshop (300 yen) is the hands-on highlight. Sign up at the information desk immediately — it fills up first on weekends.
Most explanation panels have English translations. Download the audio guide app before you come.
The kutani porcelain section has a digital coloring activity — kids design their own plate on a touchscreen and see it 'fired' on screen.
Combine with the nearby Kanazawa Castle Park and 21st Century Museum of Contemporary Art.
The museum shop sells craft kits (gold leaf bookmark sets for 500 yen) that make great hands-on souvenirs.

parentStory.title: My 6-year-old now knows more about gold leaf than I do
parentStory.excerpt: She applied gold leaf to a lacquer box at the workshop and spent the next week explaining the 24k gold process to everyone. I learned more about Ishikawa's crafts in one afternoon here than in a month of travel guides.
parentStory.author: David, dad of 1 from Auckland
parentStory.fullStory: I was worried this would be a stuffy museum with 'don't touch' signs everywhere. Instead, my daughter got to apply real gold leaf to a box. The museum brilliantly balances education with hands-on fun. The digital plate-coloring activity on the tablet kept my other kid busy for 20 minutes. We came for 1 hour, stayed for 3.

itineraryComparison.halfDay: Main exhibits + gold leaf workshop + cafe, 2 hours
itineraryComparison.fullDay: Add Kanazawa Castle + 21st Century Museum + Omicho Market lunch
itineraryComparison.bestFor: Ages 5-14, crafty kids, families wanting hands-on cultural experiences

name: Nikko National Park Family Hike
description: A stunning national park of ancient cedar forests, waterfalls, and volcanic lakes. The famous Kegon Falls drops 97 meters, while Lake Chuzenji offers pedal boats and a lakeside promenade. Easy walking trails like the Senjogahara boardwalk are stroller-friendly and perfect for little explorers.
bestTime: Late September-November (autumn colors) or June-July (green season)
tipsAndTricks: The Senjogahara boardwalk trail is 2.5km of flat wooden path — perfect for strollers and little legs. Takes about 1 hour with photo stops.
Skip the Kegon Falls elevator if you have a toddler who hates enclosed spaces. Instead view from the free observation area at the top (less crowded, better views).
Bring jackets even in summer. At 1,200m elevation, Lake Chuzenji is 8-10 degrees cooler than Nikko town.
Feed the ducks at Lake Chuzenji — there's a 100 yen pellet machine near the boat rental dock.
Pack a picnic. The upscale restaurant Chugushi Tei is the only lunch option near the lake and fills up by noon.

parentStory.title: The boardwalk where she spotted her first wild monkey
parentStory.excerpt: A Japanese macaque sat on the Senjogahara boardwalk grooming its baby. My 5-year-old froze, then whispered 'Mama, we're in a nature documentary.' We stayed 45 minutes watching that family.
parentStory.author: Sarah, mom of 2 from Toronto
parentStory.fullStory: Nikko was our escape from Tokyo's crowds and it delivered exactly what we needed. The boardwalk is so flat my 3-year-old walked the entire 2.5km without being carried. My older one counted 7 different butterfly species. Kegon Falls is thunderously loud — bring ear defenders if your kid is noise-sensitive. We spent 5 hours in the park and could have easily spent more.

itineraryComparison.halfDay: Kegon Falls + Lake Chuzenji stroll + lunch, 3 hours
itineraryComparison.fullDay: Senjogahara boardwalk + Ryuzu Falls + Lake cruise + shrine visit
itineraryComparison.bestFor: Ages 4-14, nature-loving families, day-trippers from Tokyo

name: Nikko Edomura
description: A living Edo-period village theme park where samurai, ninjas, and townspeople in period costume roam the streets. Kids can try shuriken throwing, dress in full samurai armor, watch geisha dances and ninja shows, and even ride in a palanquin carried by 'servants.'
bestTime: Weekdays, October-November when autumn colors frame the village perfectly
tipsAndTricks: The 'Oiran Parade' (courtesan procession) at 2 PM is the day's highlight. Stake out a spot on the main street by 1:45 PM.
Samurai armor rental costs 2,000 yen and includes dressing assistance. Takes 15 minutes to get them suited up — do it during the 11 AM lull.
The ninja house maze is dark with moving walls. Test your kid by going in first before taking them — some toddlers get scared.
Edo-mura street food: try the Mitarashi dango (sweet rice skewers) and Inarizushi (stuffed tofu pouches). Kid-approved.
Combine with a morning at Toshogu Shrine — they're only 15 minutes apart by car.

parentStory.title: My daughter wore samurai armor for 4 straight hours
parentStory.excerpt: She refused to take off the samurai armor even to eat. She walked around the village bowing to strangers and saying 'Gozaimasu.' A real actor-samurai bowed back and gave her a pretend sword. Best $20 we ever spent.
parentStory.author: Ken, dad of 2 from Singapore
parentStory.fullStory: Edomura is like a Japanese Renaissance fair but way more immersive. The actors stay in character 100% of the time — a 'town crier' announced our arrival when we entered. The ninja show uses real wire stunts and fire effects. My wife had her hair styled geisha-style at the costume rental. Four hours flew by like one.

itineraryComparison.halfDay: Ninja show + costume rental + village stroll + shuriken toss, 3 hours
itineraryComparison.fullDay: All shows + ninja maze + samurai experience + dinner show
itineraryComparison.bestFor: Ages 5-13, ninja/samurai fans, cultural immersion seekers

name: Matsumoto Castle Family Tour
description: Japan's oldest surviving five-tiered castle, known as the 'Crow Castle' for its striking black-and-white exterior. Inside, families can climb steep original wooden staircases, see samurai armor displays, and enjoy English audio guides that bring feudal Japan to life for kids.
bestTime: Weekday mornings (opens 8:30 AM), April-May or October-November
tipsAndTricks: The stairs inside are VERY steep (60-degree angles). Kids under 5 may need to be carried. Consider a baby carrier — strollers must be left at the entrance.
Rent the English audio guide (300 yen) — it has a kid-friendly mode with shorter explanations and sound effects.
The view from the top floor is worth the climb. On clear days you can see the Japanese Alps.
Arrive right at 8:30 AM opening — the castle is much less crowded and the morning light is perfect for photos.
The grounds are free and open before the castle opens. Let kids run wild on the grass before tackling the interior.

parentStory.title: He climbed a 400-year-old castle like a mountain
parentStory.excerpt: My 6-year-old counted every step to the top. 231 steps. He was proud of himself at each floor. The samurai armor displays on the 3rd floor stopped him in his tracks — he stood there imagining battles.
parentStory.author: Mika, mom of 1 from Yokohama
parentStory.fullStory: Matsumoto Castle is the real deal. No reconstructions, no elevators, no gimmicks. The original wooden pillars still have axe marks from 400 years ago. My son loved the 'moon-viewing platform' on the 4th floor. The staff gave him a sticker for making it to the top. We spent 2 hours inside, then another hour playing on the lawns.

itineraryComparison.halfDay: Castle interior + grounds + museum + lunch, 3 hours
itineraryComparison.fullDay: Castle morning + Matsumoto City Museum + Nawate Street shopping + sake tasting
itineraryComparison.bestFor: Ages 5-12, history-loving families, day-trip from Nagano/Tokyo

name: Hiroshima Castle & Shukkeien Garden
description: A reconstructed samurai castle surrounded by a beautiful moat, paired with Shukkeien Garden — a 400-year-old 'shrunken landscape' garden with koi ponds, bridges, and tea house. The castle has interactive exhibits and great city views, while the garden is a serene escape with paths perfect for little walkers.
tipsAndTricks: Visit Shukkeien FIRST (opens 9 AM). It's calm and uncrowded in the morning — koi are most active and kids can feed them for 100 yen.
The castle has a small museum with samurai swords and armor on the 3rd floor. Kids can touch a replica katana (supervised).
Don't climb to the top floor with a sleeping toddler — the stairs are steep and narrow like Matsumoto Castle.
Shukkeien has a tea ceremony experience for 500 yen. Kids get served matcha and a sweet that even picky eaters love.
Combine with the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Park — it's only a 15-minute walk through the city center.

parentStory.title: The garden that saved our Hiroshima trip from crying kids
parentStory.excerpt: After the Peace Museum (heavy for a 6-year-old), Shukkeien was the perfect reset. Koi fish, turtles, stepping stones, and matcha. She was laughing again within 10 minutes.
parentStory.author: Carlos, dad of 1 from Mexico City
parentStory.fullStory: We planned to spend an hour at Shukkeien as an afterthought before leaving Hiroshima. We stayed 3 hours. The garden is designed as a miniature representation of famous Japanese landscapes — the kids didn't care about that, but they loved the stepping-stone bridges across the pond. The castle from the outside is stunning against the sky. A perfect calm morning destination.

itineraryComparison.halfDay: Castle grounds + Shukkeien Garden + teahouse, 2.5-3 hours
itineraryComparison.fullDay: Add Peace Park + Museum + Okonomiyaki lunch in downtown Hiroshima
itineraryComparison.bestFor: Ages 2-12, families needing a calm break, spring visitors

name: Sapporo Maruyama Zoo
description: Sapporo's beloved city zoo located within Maruyama Park, famous for its polar bears, snow leopards, and winter animal viewing areas. The zoo redesigned enclosures specifically for Hokkaido's harsh winters, letting visitors see animals being active in the snow. A petting zoo, reptile house, and spacious park grounds make it a full-day family destination.
bestTime: Winter mornings (animals most active in cold) or June-August (pleasant weather)
tipsAndTricks: Go in the morning during winter (9:30 AM opening). The polar bears are most active when it's below zero — they swim and play in snow.
The 'contact zoo' (petting area) is indoors and heated. Perfect for warming up for 20 minutes on a cold day.
Winter entrance fee (December-March) is reduced by 30%. It's already cheap at 800 yen for adults.
Combine with Hokkaido Shrine and Maruyama Park — both are a 5-minute walk and share the same leafy grounds.
The zoo is on a hill. Enter at the top gate (via bus) and walk DOWN through the zoo — saves climbing with a stroller.

parentStory.title: The polar bear who tapped the glass to say hello
parentStory.excerpt: In -5 degree weather, a polar bear swam right up to the glass and tapped it with her paw. Our toddler tapped back. They 'talked' for 10 minutes through the glass. Worth the cold.
parentStory.author: Anna, mom of 2 from Helsinki
parentStory.fullStory: Coming from Finland, I wasn't sure a zoo in Hokkaido's winter would be special. It was. The polar bear exhibit is incredible — underwater viewing windows show them swimming above you. The snow monkey enclosure has a hot spring they bathe in during winter (adorable). We bundled up and spent 3 hours outside without anyone complaining. The heated indoor areas are perfectly spaced.

itineraryComparison.halfDay: Zoo + petting corner + polar bear exhibit + Maruyama Park, 3 hours
itineraryComparison.fullDay: Zoo morning + Hokkaido Shrine + Odori Park + Sapporo Ramen Alley lunch
